## Summary

Upgrade desktop and remote from **Copilot SDK `1.0.18-preview.1` / runtime `1.0.94-1`** to exact **`1.0.18-preview.3` / `1.0.94-3`**, the newest npm prerelease when this request was resolved. Stable `latest` remains `1.0.17` and is not selected.

Fresh branch from main **`ddcb6c27affe30052a2ade0bfe6c8bcaea9f89e5`**, after [#340406](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340406) merged. This PR makes **no host production-code, UI, setting/policy, or product-telemetry changes**. The previous upgrade's typed Auto-tier adaptation, positive OTel concurrency assertions, native skill prompt baselines, canonical temporary-directory helper, and proven Kerberos fixture prerequisite are already on main and remain unchanged.

This PR remains **draft**. The complete local candidate suite, all GitHub workflows, and **both packaged Windows/Linux/macOS Azure builds passed on the exact final revision**. Initial sleep-interrupted local runs, Marketplace-503 failures, and post-test scanner timeouts are disclosed separately, not reported as initial passes.

## Change ledger

All **six changed files**:

| Files/surface | Exact change | Why necessary | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, `remote/package.json`, `remote/package-lock.json` (4) | Exact SDK preview 3/runtime `1.0.94-3` pins and regenerated SDK/eight optional platform entries in both locks | Matching release on desktop and remote | Expected dependency upgrade; installed root/remote SDK/runtime, both lock roots, platform pins, and unchanged unrelated entries verified |
| `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/KNOWN_ISSUES.md` (1) | Update still-reproduced native inherited-identity defect to SDK preview 3/runtime `1.0.94-3` and immutable predicate permalink | Keep active failure evidence aligned with the bundle | Existing assertion/expected-failure marker unchanged; no new gate or skip |
| `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/README.md` (1) | Update passing no-restart managed-telemetry runtime evidence | Keep the current test contract accurate | Related documentation only |

**No generated fixture or prompt baseline changed.** All 19 model-family prompt baselines pass strict replay unchanged, including model set, tool inventory/order/schema, sampling, and complete normalized request bodies. No normalization, stale-request exception, test deadline, assertion, or skip was weakened.

## Exact release provenance and review

Inspected/shipped revisions, not claimed introducing commits:

- Baseline `cli-1.0.94-1`: **`44097658e184184613f404efe56e6c4d3a991656`**.
- Candidate `cli-1.0.94-3` and `sdk-1.0.18-preview.3`: **`d8cd60bc89ed3ae60cc37d7877021ac49bd52492`**.

Complete immutable Git inventory: **24 commits / 253 files**, including **93 runtime files / seven Node SDK files**. Patch review was risk-focused, not a claim of exhaustive review. The three production Node SDK files change **59 insertions / five deletions**:

- Optional `fileEdits` complete UTF-8 before/after previews on write-permission requests. Existing path/diff fields and host confirmation behavior remain usable; this PR does not introduce a new preview UI.
- Optional `workspaces.diff.includeContents`, default false, and before/after display contents. Existing capture/read limits and binary/unavailable-content exclusions remain. This PR does not request the new surface or treat text previews as a file-restore contract.
- Internal workflow constant renaming, without behavior change.

Native OTel implementation, proxy/network implementation, and managed-settings schema are unchanged between the bundled revisions. The still-failing inherited `user.name` redaction predicate continues to match only `process.user.name` and `host.name`.

### Notable runtime changes and review concerns

- **MCP resilience:** servers refusing, timing out, or partially acknowledging `subscriptions/listen` remain usable with only acknowledged delivery trusted; live catalogs re-list where delivery is unsupported. Authentication/HTTP exchange failures and closed/canceled transports remain fatal rather than being concealed. Hunter Sadler's [github/copilot-agent-runtime#25098](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/25098).
- **408 recovery:** retain timeout counting across intervening transport failures and preserve reasoning on every adjacent assistant chunk of the still-in-flight response, rather than only its last message. Julián Bayardo Spadafora's [github/copilot-agent-runtime#25414](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/25414) and [github/copilot-agent-runtime#25423](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/25423).
- **Managed resume and approvals:** generation-fenced, serialized client-policy resume transactions and rollback avoid stale permission restoration; determined policy revocation of Allow All emits a runtime-owned warning. CLI policy-helper-before-plugin-activation work is distinguished from native host behavior; VS Code adds no duplicate enforcement.
- **Default-on Anthropic refusal fallback:** [github/copilot-agent-runtime#25340](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/25340), introduced by shibbas on October 7, removes the experiment gate. Eligible refused requests can be reissued against a distinct configured fallback and continue on that model. This is a substantive upstream behavior change, not just a type expansion; replay here does **not** exercise a live refusal/fallback or prove real-model quality.
- **Search guidance:** [github/copilot-agent-runtime#23017](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/23017) more strongly prefers a search subagent when that tool is present. The existing Agent Host request baselines remain unchanged under its host-owned prompt/tool configuration; this does not prove real-model behavioral equivalence.
- **Staff-only native process-assurance observation:** [github/copilot-agent-runtime#19923](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/19923) adds telemetry-only observation of tool events, gated by the runtime's `Staff` feature availability and telemetry destination/session enablement. It does not change tools/model behavior. No VS Code telemetry producer or classification is modified, but this is **not** a claim that all native runtime telemetry is unchanged.
- **Publication ordering:** Mackinnon Buck's October 7 [github/copilot-agent-runtime#25419](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/25419), commit `48d9895da944fd191a06f7e059c0691d3b33bcb3`, makes normal internal mirrors depend on successful public SDK publication. This addresses the earlier release-workflow ordering hazard; it does not retroactively repair stable `1.0.17`'s immutable feed artifact.

## Package integrity

Actual authenticated Azure-feed archives were downloaded and hashed:

- SDK preview 3: **595,262 bytes**, SHA-512 **`8VfzBRIuhYmxvwEEsFMkpLqisxUjW1I7lxn2EsSJXj1Wlr+yrQe1wjXxEBDygQJeedMK/Dtc5tQEKndx/KiUBQ==`**, matching public npm metadata.
- Darwin arm64 preview 3: **54,360,060 bytes**, SHA-512 **`hxSXGzGnOrtQH6j7ull6OqJdN7JBofLejZJbf/hNnRB7dkBuaSbYIyDes4NyA2pynhTo3cVipibjfAdJ2MyGGg==`**, matching public npm metadata.
- Other platform integrity remains enforced by npm and packaged Windows/Linux validation. No feed write, registry override, credential change, or hand-edited integrity hash was used.

## Exact candidate local validation

SDK `1.0.18-preview.3` / runtime `1.0.94-3`, host base `ddcb6c27affe30052a2ade0bfe6c8bcaea9f89e5`, macOS arm64. Output compilation did not overlap tests.

| Exact command | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm install` | Passed plain root install including remote; installed manifests, lock roots/eight platform pins, and unchanged unrelated dependency entries verified |
| `npm run build-fast -- --client-only` | Passed |
| `npm run typecheck-client` | Passed without host adaptation |
| `npm run gulp check-package-json` / `git diff --check` | Passed |
| `caffeinate -is npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --jobs 1` | **950 passing / 111 existing pending**, all six complete final summaries, **1,011.9 seconds**. The sleep-interrupted initial runs and unchanged recovery are disclosed below |
| `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --runGlob '**/agentHost/test/node/{providerIntegration/*,e2e/providers/copilotPromptsE2E,e2e/providers/codexAgentHostLive}.integrationTest.js'` | **72 passing / six existing live-only pending**, all nine synthetic provider suites plus strict prompt replay |
| `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSdkCanvas.integrationTest.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSdkImportSession.integrationTest.ts` | **Three passing** |
| `env -u COPILOT_HOME VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgentSession.test.ts` | **1,594 passing / one existing Windows-only pending** |

### Initial full-run timeouts and recovery

The first six-entrypoint run produced complete passing summaries for conformance (368/15), Claude (124/38), Codex (153/34), and managed settings (15/0), but failed:

- Copilot `resumes a failed turn in place`: 267 passing / 24 pending / one timeout.
- Native OTel `provider turn exports SDK spans through the Agent Host file exporter`: 21 passing / one timeout.

Both exceeded their existing 180-second test deadlines. Host/runtime logs were inspected first; they show model responses and native usage/event delivery, but do not establish why final lifecycle settlement stalled. No SDK-specific root cause or “infrastructure-only” classification is claimed.

Fresh-process reproduction with unchanged assertions:

- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotOtelAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep 'resumes a failed turn in place|cold resume'`: **Four passing**, including the exact resume failure and three cold-resume cases.
- `VSCODE_SKIP_PRELAUNCH=1 ./scripts/test-integration.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/providers/copilotOtelAgentHostE2E.integrationTest.ts --grep 'provider turn exports SDK spans through the Agent Host file exporter'`: **One passing**.
- Second complete unchanged `npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --jobs 1`: **failed**, **945 passing / 111 pending / five timeouts**, **3,223.3 seconds**. Conformance had three timeouts in historical Git-blob reading, sync/push completion, and restoring a discarded deleted file; Copilot had timeouts in bounded chat-attachment history and a custom subagent. The first run's exact resume and file-exporter cases passed in this second run. No assertion, deadline, fixture, or gate was changed.

Read-only macOS power logs establish that these local runs repeatedly crossed system sleep/deep-idle intervals. Their wake timestamps match the previously unexplained host/runtime gaps: the file-exporter run paused from **22:25:22 to 22:40:09**, and the second run's attachment/subagent logs resumed at **23:20:24 / 23:33:58**, matching system dark-wake transitions after sleep at **23:13:57 / 23:22:01**. A local `git rev-parse` also exceeded its existing five-second deadline at a wake transition. These are not evidence of a deterministic candidate model/permission failure.

`caffeinate -is npm run test-agent-host-e2e -- --jobs 1` ran the **same complete suite** with a temporary sleep-prevention assertion scoped to that command's lifetime and **passed 950 / 111 existing pending**, all six final summaries, **1,011.9 seconds**: conformance 368/15, Claude 124/38, Codex 153/34, Copilot 268/24, native OTel 22/0, managed settings 15/0. No permanent power setting, test deadline, assertion, source, or fixture changed. The active assertion was verified during execution and its owned process was absent after completion. GitHub's complete exact-candidate macOS suite separately passed **950 / 111**, including both original timeout cases and enabled/disabled OTel concurrency.

## Exact revision cloud validation

- Source SHA: **`2a8ee1f24f62901f25a507b519d491257187d9df`**; signed commit's normal verification hook ran successfully (zero eligible TypeScript files in this dependency/documentation-only diff).
- New **draft** [#340441](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/340441). GitHub Code OSS [37734061441](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/actions/runs/37734061441) and all applicable secondary workflows **passed**.
- Packaged Azure definition 111 [482081](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=482081) / [482082](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=482082): both authoritative build records report **completed / succeeded**, source **`2a8ee1f24f62901f25a507b519d491257187d9df`**, verified. Every final stage succeeded. Normal trusted feed, CI mode, Windows/Linux x64 and actual pipeline macOS arm64, tests enabled, publication/release disabled.
- Both original fresh builds actually executed all six provider suites and positive native OTel controls on every supported platform; Linux also executed the required disk-backed lifecycle pass. Later infrastructure retries reused successful checkpoints where applicable and are not counted as additional actual E2E executions.
- PR remains **draft and conflict-free** after final verification. No ready/merge action, approval override, force-push, or upstream merge was performed.

Both initial queue attempts were rejected for unavailable Azure CLI authentication. Existing Azure account state was checked and its normal token-refresh command restored authenticated CLI reads; no credential/registry configuration was changed. A branch build-list check confirmed no duplicate builds, and the same two nonpublishing queue commands then succeeded with the IDs above.

The second Azure build's Quality stage failed while downloading the existing `ms-vscode.js-debug` VSIX: Marketplace returned **HTTP 503 on ten retries**. Its unchanged completed-stage retry **passed**. Its Linux remote integration task also reported **335 passing / 55 pending / one failure** because the server-installed test extension was absent. The preserved server log shows **“Error while installing extensions: Server returned 503”** for the test resolver's `ms-vscode.vscode-smoketest-check` install; this is not an SDK permission or Agent Host assertion failure. Its unchanged completed-stage retry **passed**, including the exact formerly failing server-CLI extension assertion and full API folder batch (**336 passing / 55 existing pending**). Successful prior test checkpoints were reused where applicable; actual repeated E2E coverage comes from the two original independent builds, not skipped retry tasks.

Both original fresh packaged builds executed all supported platforms, with all six final summaries and the original positive native OTel concurrency assertions:

| Platform | Actual full E2E totals in each fresh build | Additional execution |
|---|---|---|
| Windows x64 | **916 passing / 145 existing pending**: conformance 364/19, Claude 122/40, Codex 153/34, Copilot 240/52, OTel 22/0, managed settings 15/0 | Enabled/disabled native OTel concurrency passed the original 288 real-shell-call, four event-producer, per-RPC progress, span, and clean-shutdown assertions |
| macOS arm64 | **950 passing / 111 existing pending** | Positive native OTel controls and the original authenticated Kerberos PAC task passed in both builds |
| Linux x64 | **950 passing / 111 existing pending** in tmpfs replay | **18 passing / zero pending** actual disk-backed lifecycle cases: conformance 6, Claude 4, Codex 4, Copilot 4; OTel/managed settings zero selected intentionally in the disk grep. Positive native OTel controls passed |

Those are two actual executions per supported platform, not checkpoint-skipped retries. Native OTel concurrency's overall Windows duration around 15 seconds is distinct from the unchanged per-RPC 15-second bound.

Both Windows stages subsequently hit the unchanged **50-minute job limit** during post-test security processing: first `Guardian: TSAUpload`, second `Guardian: PREfast`. Normal unchanged completed-stage retries with `forceRetryAllJobs:false` **passed in both builds**, producing the verified overall `succeeded` results above. Passed-test checkpoints were reused where applicable; no source, assertion, job deadline, or gate changed. Application-test success was not treated as overall build success before those final authoritative results.

## Remaining limitations

- Native inherited `user.name` redaction remains an exact expected failure, along with historical binary Git-blob corruption and Codex mixed-content MCP decoding. No markers or gates were added or weakened.
- The existing Kerberos fixture fix is on main and unchanged: it verifies **host utility CAPI authentication** via explicitly selected worktree branch generation, not native SDK HTTPS inference. New preview3 packaged runs must establish their own pass.
- Default native OTel batching and pre-batch shutdown observations from the previous upgrade are historical. Relevant exporter source is unchanged, but these are not relabeled as preview3 binary measurements; the candidate's actual OTel and clean-shutdown test results are separate above.
- Live credentialed Entra/authentication flows, real-model refusal fallback/steering/cancellation, and new optional diff/preview UI are not established by tokenless replay. Green replay is not evidence that this release resolves the maintainer's reported general bot-quality concerns.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install and package desktop or remote Agent Host dependencies for a supported platform
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Dependency resolution and product packaging must complete before the build is usable. The diff replaces the SDK wrapper and native runtime versions in both root and remote lockfiles but does not add dependency nodes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: package-lock.json node_modules/@github/copilot-sdk and platform package entries; remote/package-lock.json equivalent entries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve/download the @github/copilot-sdk wrapper and applicable optional native package from the npm registry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Same package-node cardinality as before: one wrapper and eight platform-qualified optional entries in each lock; effective installed native payload is target-dependent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same wrapper and same eight optional platform package entries were resolved at preview.1; the diff changes only versions, URLs, and integrity values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold dependency installation waits for the new artifacts; warm installs can use npm's integrity-addressed cache.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write dependency contents and package the selected SDK/runtime assets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected native runtime payload per target plus the SDK wrapper, unchanged from the base graph.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The preview.1 artifacts occupied the same package roles and packaging path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Build/package critical path, not editor runtime startup.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Supported target platforms and architectures. The lock retains the same SDK wrapper plus eight mutually platform-qualified optional native packages; a target consumes its matching native artifact rather than introducing per-session work.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: npm controls registry/download concurrency; this diff adds no loop, worker, limiter change, or additional independently scheduled package operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The npm content cache can serve warm installs by integrity hash; the upgraded artifacts necessarily miss an old-version cache once, then use normal npm caching. There is no application cache involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that dependency graph cardinality and platform selection are unchanged, based on complete root and remote lockfile hunks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Artifact byte sizes for every platform are not present in the reviewable diff, so a small download or disk-size delta cannot be quantified; there is no evidenced cardinality or lifecycle regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this is a one-for-one package replacement with unchanged dependency and platform fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: First desktop or remote Copilot Agent Host use and first SDK-backed session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A renderer request lazily starts the Agent Host process. The Copilot provider constructor does not start the SDK runtime; the first operation requiring `_ensureClient` resolves assets and starts one native runtime subprocess before the session can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the bundled native Copilot runtime over stdio via `RuntimeConnection.forStdio`, then await `CopilotClient.start()`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced runtime subprocess per active Copilot client generation, not one per concurrent caller or session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preview.1 used the same host lifecycle, stdio connection, and one-client coalescing; only the selected executable/package version changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold first SDK-backed operation waits for runtime startup; warm sessions reuse the client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe runtime, native module, SDK, extension, and bootstrap paths with `fs.access`.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Five parallel checks per platform candidate; one candidate on macOS/Windows and up to two on Linux.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The identical resolver probed preview.1 package paths with the same cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs on cold SDK client startup before subprocess launch, not normal editor startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initialize and communicate with the native runtime over stdio RPC.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One runtime connection multiplexes sessions and RPC operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same SDK/runtime IPC architecture and host call placement existed before the version bump.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Client start and session RPCs wait on this boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Concurrent first-use callers and Linux runtime candidates. Concurrent callers share `_ensureClientHealing`/`_clientStarting`; runtime path probing checks one platform candidate normally and at most two on Linux.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cold SDK startup is coalesced into one shared promise. Independent asset, ripgrep, telemetry, and optional override checks run in one Promise.all. Startup-config recovery is globally bounded rather than per caller.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold use probes runtime files and starts the subprocess. Warm use returns the retained `_client`; failures clear startup state and cleanup owns the subprocess. There is no changed negative-cache behavior in host code.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in host critical-path reachability, laziness, coalescing, and boundary cardinality; low confidence in unreviewable upstream implementation details, which is insufficient for a finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The internal startup cost of the opaque upgraded binary is not visible in repository source, so exact milliseconds cannot be compared. No diff evidence establishes added startup work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff neither moves SDK startup onto application startup nor increases host-side filesystem, subprocess, or IPC multiplicity.

Scenarios.Scenario: Send a normal Copilot agent turn, including model and tool activity
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A turn is queued per chat, refreshes or resumes its session if needed, then `entry.send` drives the runtime. Provider model HTTP and any requested tools must complete before the turn completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Transitive native runtime boundary documented and exercised by src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e harness and provider suites
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send model requests to Copilot API endpoints and consume streamed responses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Typically one request per simple turn, with additional requests only for existing multi-step tool/subagent/retry workflows. Unchanged strict fixtures provide no diff evidence of added requests on ordinary successful turns.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preview.1 already issued model requests for each SDK-backed turn under the same host send path and replay contract.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Model response is on the turn critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Transitive Copilot runtime tool path exercised by Agent Host E2E suites
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Execute runtime-selected shell tools or MCP server tools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Driven by model-selected tool calls; the host diff adds no tool, per-item launch, or concurrency change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same runtime/tool boundaries existed with preview.1.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous tool calls block turn completion; background behavior depends on the existing workflow.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize prompts, histories, tool schemas/results, and stdio RPC messages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per model/tool event with payload size driven by conversation and tool content; no changed host metadata or serializer is present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preview.1 received the same host session configuration and request payloads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Occurs on the turn path, but no changed allocation or cap is evidenced by the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of turns, concurrent chats/subagents, model calls requested by the workflow, and tool invocations. A normal replayed turn has the same expected model-request sequence after the upgrade.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Turns for a chat pass through the existing chat queue; independent chats/subagents may run concurrently through the shared runtime. The diff changes no host queue, limiter, or fan-out code.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm sessions reuse the live SDK client and session. Cold/resumed sessions pay existing session creation/resume work. Strict replay treats any unrecorded model request as a hard miss and requires all recorded responses to be consumed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the host request path and strict replay cardinality contract are unchanged; insufficient evidence to attribute a concrete new expensive mechanism to preview.3.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The upgraded dependency's internal source is not in the supplied diff. Conditional recovery behavior inside the runtime may differ, but there is no reviewable evidence of unbounded retries, extra requests on successful turns, or increased payload scale.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance finding. A version change alone cannot prove additional network, subprocess, or serialization cost, and unchanged replay behavior rejects speculative fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Use Copilot sessions with MCP catalogs and plugin tools
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session setup/reconciliation reads SDK MCP configuration over stdio; MCP servers may be started and their catalogs listed before tools are available. Invoked MCP tools then execute before the requesting turn proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call SDK MCP configuration/list and session RPCs over the existing stdio connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing list calls occur at session configuration/reconciliation boundaries, not newly per catalog item due to this diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same host RPC calls and placement existed with preview.1.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration reads can delay session setup or refresh.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Transitive runtime MCP path exercised by src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/suites/copilotRuntimeMcpSuite.ts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start configured MCP servers and invoke their tools through the native runtime.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per configured MCP server and selected tool invocation; no changed effective cardinality is established.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preview.1 already owned MCP server lifecycle and tool calls under the same host configuration.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalog readiness and synchronous tool results can be on session/turn critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured MCP servers, catalog changes, sessions, and tool calls. Effective cardinality is per configured server/session after existing retained snapshots and plugin-controller reconciliation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The existing shared SDK client and session/plugin controller own reconciliation. The diff changes no host-side Promise.all fan-out, limiter, subscription, or server-start loop.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live sessions retain runtime catalogs and host snapshots; cold/resumed sessions reconstruct them. The changed package may contain internal resilience behavior, but no cache invalidation or repeated-list mechanism is visible in the reviewable diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the unchanged host RPC/subprocess boundaries; insufficient confidence in any changed upstream relist frequency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Upstream MCP subscription fallback details are not present in repository code, so repeated catalog-list frequency cannot be independently established from the diff. Without that mechanism and trigger, a finding would be speculative.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no changed host fan-out or cache lifecycle is proven, and opaque package behavior is not enough to claim repeated boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Stop, restart, or shut down the Copilot runtime with telemetry enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A client restart or Agent Host shutdown waits for `CopilotClient.stop`; the host then disposes the BYOK proxy handle. Application shutdown has an existing six-second outer timeout before termination.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Gracefully stop the native runtime and, if necessary, terminate the Agent Host process after the existing timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced runtime stop per client generation and one Agent Host process shutdown per host lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preview.1 used the same stop ownership, coalescing, and timeout path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On restart it blocks creation of the replacement client; on application shutdown it is bounded by the manager timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Location: Transitive runtime telemetry path configured in src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts
ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Export runtime OpenTelemetry spans/events when telemetry is configured.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Driven by existing telemetry events/batches; the diff changes no host exporter endpoint, producer count, or flush placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Preview.1 received the same host telemetry configuration and shutdown contract.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Normal exporting is runtime-owned; final flush may participate in graceful stop, still under the existing shutdown bound.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Live sessions, in-flight turns/subagents, telemetry events, and restart frequency. One shared client stop covers the runtime generation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent stops are coalesced by `_clientStopping`; Agent Host process shutdown is joined and timeout-bounded. Telemetry producers may be concurrent, but no changed producer or batching configuration appears in the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Stopping clears prewarmed metadata, client references, pending restart reasons, and the runtime-owned proxy handle so the next start creates fresh state. No changed retained cache or missing disposal is evidenced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that cleanup ownership, stop coalescing, and process timeout are unchanged; insufficient evidence of a new runtime retention or flush mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The upgraded binary's exact telemetry flush duration and batching internals are opaque, but no changed source, failure, or benchmark demonstrates a regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable cleanup or shutdown regression is established by the package version replacement.
